headline: Approved a well at Martin Farm Property and permission to trim growth at 7 ½ Willow Street.
summary: Members discussed site plans for 63 English Range Road, Denali Estates Phase V, and 38 Jackman Road, but took no votes on them. They approved a well at the Martin Farm Property. The Town Council tabled the Community Wildfire Protection Plan to give the public more time to review it.
decisions: Approved the minutes of August 17, 2026 by unanimous vote.
Approved the Rapid Response Emergency Subcommittee minutes of August 24, 2026 by unanimous vote.
Accepted the $19.00 donation from the Hannaford for Good Program to be kept in the Land Preservation account by unanimous vote.
Approved permitting the applicant to move forward with installing a well within the agricultural purposes of the easement by unanimous vote.
Approved a $70 reimbursement to Commissioner Chabot for NHACC annual meeting registration by unanimous vote.
Approved allowing the resident at 7 ½ Willow Street to trim back the property with non-motorized gardening tools by unanimous vote.
Town Council voted to table adoption of the Community Wildfire Protection Plan.

decision_evidence.quote: Commissioner Metts MOVED to approve the Minutes of August 17, 2026. Commissioner Spoerl seconded the Motion. Vote: Unanimous
Commissioner Chabot MOVED to approve the Rapid Response Emergency Subcommittee Meeting Minutes of August 24, 2026. Robert Spoerl seconded the Motion. Vote: Unanimous
Commissioner Metts made a MOTION to accept the $19.00 donation from the Hannaford for Good Program to be kept in the Land Preservation account. Eileen Chabot seconded the Motion. Vote: Unanimous

Commissioner Spoerl MOTIONEDto permit the applicant to move forward with the processandinstall a well that falls within the agriculture purposes of the easement. Commissioner Metts seconded the Motion. Vote: Unanimous

Commissioner Metts MOVEDto approve $70 reimbursement to Commissioner Chabot for the NHACC Annual meeting registration cost out of the Administration Account. Commissioner Spoerl seconded the Motion. Vote: Unanimous

Commissioner Metts MOVEDtoallow the resident who hascurrently asked permission to trim back 7 ½ Willow Street access use of hedge trimmers, weedwhackers and any other non-motorized gardening utensils to trim said property back. Commissioner Comrie seconded the Motion. Vote: Unanimous
The Council voted to table the vote to adopt it to give the public more time to review the document.

-The Commission receivedreported violationsfrom the Department of Environmental Servicesat 25

-SitePlan Review:
-Tax Map 11092, Lot 001; 63 English Range Road; 13 Lot Subdivision; Owner: RGNH Construction-Kevin Landry,
20 Rockingham Rd, Windham NH.Surveyor: James Verra & Associates, Inc,(JVA) 100 GriffinRoad Unit C,
Portsmouth, NH. Presenters: Nicholas DiBartholomeo, Morgan Moody, Kevin Landry, and Ryan Fowler.
NicholasDiBartholomeo and Morgan Moodystate the land isa 43-lotparcel.Of the 43 lots,they willonly be
disturbing1300 square feetof wetlands.The currentplan includesa 13-lotsubdivisionwith 3,300 linearfeetof
road whereit willhave a vertical,granitecurbingculvertsystem thatgoesto 4 differentponds. Mr.
DiBartholomeohighlighted on the drawing wherethe road willcome infrom ScenicDriveand showed whereit
willdisturbwetlands.Thefirst incompact from the roadis at 1,265 feetand another pointof impact at40
squarefeet. Inthe northeasternareaof thesite iswhere the highervaluewetlandis locatedwithinthe 100-
year floodarea. Much ofthe proposed subdivisiondoes not reach toward thiswetland area.The wetland area
and vernalpoolswereflagged inMarch and April2026 and the wetland functionsand valuesassessmentfor
New Hampshire Department of Environmental Serviceswas completed. Theplan is currentlyinthe
environmental review processinregardto the vernalpools and the possiblehabitatfragmentationwithinthe
proposedsubdivision. The majorityof the wetlands are forestedwetlands with a few emergent wetlands along
the powerline corridor.The smallerwetland area isdisturbedby an accompanyingtrail alongsideitthatexists.
Chairman Buzzanga inquiredabout a pipe noted onthe plans. Itwas noted to be 134 feetlong and 12 inches
wide. The culvertisproposed. Chairman Buzzanga confirmed thatthe wetland the roadis going through wasa
continuous wetland andthe pipe willkeep itcontinuous.It willbe a pipe with outletprotection,and a ripwrap
apron to slow downany velocities. The pipe willbe located6 feetunder the road.Commissioner Chabot asked
to see the setof plansthatincludesthe gradinglinesas gradingisimportant to wetland’simpact.
Commissioner Metts asked when they return,he would liketo see the plans’septicsas wellas the setbacks.
Commissioner Chabotalso statedthatthe updated plansshould be stamped bya certifiedWetland Scientist
along with a descriptionof the wetlands and labeledon the plan.Chairman Buzzanga statedthatthey would
schedule a futuresitewalk and a setof planswould be madeavailable priorto the walk.Chairman Buzzanga
alsoasked them to review thesize of the pipe and speak with Town of Derry Deputy PublicWorks Director
Mark L’Heureux concerningits current plannedsize.
Site Plan Review:
-Tax Map 14, Lot 15: 22.5 Overledge Drive; Phase V Subdivision; Owner: JAL, LLC 5 Madden Road,Derry, NH;
Presenters: Michael P.Butler,PE and Brent J.Cole, PE.
-BrentCole of GraniteEngineeringintroducedhimselfas the engineer of the projectand was accompanied by
Tom Lannan ofJAL,LLC. They are presentingDenaliEstatesPhase V.Priorphases brought beforethisBoard
had smallerwetland impacts.The overview plan iscoming inoffof Danieland ForestRoads whichbring Phases
|and IVtogether.The futuredevelopmentof Phase V takes ForestRoad and extendsit intothe vacant land
thatisthere.They are proposing 20 lotson a town-maintained road whichis essentiallyForestStreet
Extension.Phase VI isnot being proposedcurrently. Theirobjectivenow isto provide a preliminaryoverview
and answerhigh levelquestionsregardingPhase V.They wouldlike to schedule a sitewalk as they are
scheduled to go beforethe TechnicalReview Committee and returnto the Commission with a fullydeveloped
plan set.There are two wetland crossings.They have met with townofficials,includingthe Zoning Board,on
thisprojectand have beenvetted by the Townof Derry.The town has beeninvolved inthe design process
itself.Mr. Cole has had extensiveconversationswith the Department of Environmental Servicesregardingthe
two wetland crossings.They have alsospoken with N.H. Fishand Game about endangered speciesand how
they can help to mitigatewith theirplans.The wetlands are not stream crossingsbut forestedwetlandsthat
drainfrom north to south downto the largerwetland complex. They are carryingthe 25 foot no cut bufferthat
has been appliedto the entireprojector at leastthe former Phases.
The currentplansshow a 4,600 square footwetland impact thatwillincludea crossculvert.Currentlyit isa 48-
inchconcrete pipe.Inthe past,the Stateof New Hampshire has requested to have a 48-inch RCP pipe ona
non-stream wetland crossing.Mr. Cole explained“stream simulation.”The plan includeshead walls.Mr.
Lannanrecalled using organics in Phase |.The second wetland impact isabout a 3,000 square foot impact. The
48-inchwidth pipes are about 150 feetlong. A nativewildlifemix willbe used forthe steep slopesnear the
wetlands.Conversationensued regardinghow surfacesandfilterswillbe used and how they work. Regulations
in Derry as well as alterationterrain require allthe impervious areas to not only be treated but mitigated and a
portionof itto be recharged back intothe aquifer.A second sandfilter ison the plansas well.Commission
Spoerl asked whowill maintain thefilters over time and Mr. Cole replied the town maintains them. The goalin
designingthese systemsis thatthey don’tfail,they are designed forthe 100-year storm.Theyare builtwith
broadcasted weirs so ifthe outletstructureisoverwhelmed thereis path foritto go thatdoesn’t necessarily
drainintoanyone’s backyards and drainsback to the wetlands. Maintenance isminimal and they are checked
annually.They are to be mowed twice a year.A futuresitewalk isplanned on this80-acre parcel.The wetlands
have beenrecently flagged.
-SitePlan Review:
-Tax Map 7 Lot 77; 38 Jackman Road/Jackman Road Right-of-Way; Owner: Joe Mastriano, 3 BallAvenue, Salem,
N.H. 03079; Engineer: EngineerAlliance, Inc.,194 Central Street,Saugus, MA 01906,Presenters: Eric
Bradanese,P.E.
Owner Joe Mastriano and EricBradanese, PE (who attended virtually.)Mr. Bradanese reminded the
Commission hehad first presented the plan inAugust 2026 with preliminaryplansfor thisproject.There have
been some minorrevisions sincethe planwasfirst presented.They were taskedwith gettingmore wetlands
informationthat needsto be put on the planssuch as the date of the wetland flagging,and the types of
wetlands which they have nowreceived from Bruce Gilday,Wetland Scientist.That informationwas added to
the plan sheets.They alsoadded the 75-footno cut bufferto the prime wetland to show what impact they
mayhave in that area.One item from the Town EngineeringDepartment wasto adjustsome of the roadway
gradingforthe proposedculvert thatwillrun under Jackman Roadright-of-way.The scopeof this projectisto
builda single-familydwellingand a garage with an Accessory DwellingUnit (ADU) aboveit. Jackman Roadis a
Class6 Road that isnot maintained by the Townof Derry.There isa portionof the road maintained by an
abutterto thissite.The last625 feetthat leadsto the frontageof the propertywould be maintained by Mr.
Mastriano.This willbe constructedas a 20-foot-widegravelroad.Thiswas coordinatedwith Town engineering
and the FireDepartmentto assurethatthey have maintained enough accessboth horizontallyand vertically.
Thisensures the roadway grades and stormwater workefficiently.Thisroad willprovidea significantstorage
volume forstormwaterimpacts. Chairman Buzzanga confirmed the 60 feethe saw onthe plans is between the
added boulders and the edge of the wetland. Mr. Bradanesestated there isno directimpact on the wetland.
-Commissioner Chabot expressed some concerns she noted on September14, 2026. Work had alreadybegun
as she saw a largemachine working and noted treeshad alreadybeen cut.She was pleasedto see silt fence
had beenerected but wasnot sureit was putin the rightplace interms of the 75-footsetbackto the prime
wetland. She also stated she wasnot pleased to know the plan showed only 60-feet distance from the
wetland. She reminded the Commission thatthe standard is75-feetsetback from a prime wetland. Mr.
Mastriano agreed thatsomesite prep work had been done with sometree clearingintothe proposed house
area.He statedhe avoided the wetland area.Mr. Bradanese shared that he had discussionswith a Compliance
Specialistnamed Sephera M. Michailidesatthe N.H. Department of Environmental Services.He saidhe sent
the plansto her and the Department had no specificconcerns.Mr. Bradanese explainedthe propertyfrontage
forthesite isbasicallyentirelywithinthe 150-footbufferto the prime wetland. Thisarea of concern was a
requestto have the hammer head turn aroundfor fire access.The totalimpact from the edge of roadwayall
the way throughthe site wherethe building isgoing to be is77,000 square feet.Discussionensued regarding
seekingrelief from the setbackfrom the Department of Environmental Services.Beth Carver,Land Manager,
added she spoke with the Derry Code Enforcement Officerwho confirmed work had ceasedat the location.Mr.
Bradaneseoffered hisapologies,statingitwas a misunderstanding regardingthe preparationwork thatwas
doneon the site. Chairman Buzzanga asked thatthe cornerof interestthey had spoken about would be
flaggedpriorto a scheduled sitewalk and reminded everyone the prime wetland area must remaininits
existingconditions.Chairman Buzzangashared thatthe Commission willschedule a sitewalk soon.
-Well at Martin Farm Property,NutfieldFarms LLC presenting:Andrew Chisholm of 70 Old Auburn Road spoke
of acquiringthe property inJune of 2025. He explainedhowthe existing wellon the propertyisacrossthe
streetatthe Pinegree property.They have the pumpin theirhouse, and the wellison the propertythat he
owns. The water comesfrom the wellintothe house and then flowsinto a pipe underthe streetover to the
barn.Dueto the ledge,it isonly about 8 inchesdeep andfreezes inthe winter.There isno year-round water
accessto the barn.Theyintend to restartthe dairyoperation.He has reached out to the United States
Departmentof Agriculture(U.S.D.A.)and the NaturalResources ConservationService(N.R.C.S.),and they have
approveda projectfor the farm.It willbe funded by the N.R.C.S.as a projectunderthe U.S.D.A.Infollowingall
the U.S.D.A. guidelines he willcontract with Skillingsand Sons, LLC to do the well. He provided a picture of the
locationof the proposed well.
 
Commissioner SpoerlMOTIONED to permit the applicantto move forward with the processand install a

The Community WildfireProtectionPlan was presented to the Town Councilon September15, 2026. The

-Other Business:Chairman Buzzanga spoke of the upcomingsite walks that need to be scheduled.He

At 9:06 p.m.,Commissioner Metts MOVED to adjourn.Commissioner Chabot seconded the Motion.
